en: Yep! We'll pass it this time, too!

Nothin' beats good comedy! Just say the word if ya ever feel like doin' some more!

Yes, that'd be great.
All right! Which topic'll we go with?
Let's try relationships.
Okay! Let's head to the practice area and give it a shot!
Let's try dreams.
Let's try hobbies.
Sorry, I think I'll pass, actually.
Gotcha. Well, if you ever get the urge, say the word.

Yeah, I've shot five locations.

Please come back and visit Tsukimino again.

Excuse me, do you have a minute?
Hmm? Whaddya want?
I'm from the Tsukimino Tourism Board. Right now we're running a campaign to raise Tsukimino's profile as a tourist destination.
An advertising campaign? Sounds like a good idea.
Yes. I'd like to ask you to take some photos of places around Tsukimino that you think are must-see landmarks.
The photos you take will be used in pamphlets and posters promoting Tsukimino as a tourist destination.
If you can shoot five sightseeing spots for me, I'll give you a fabulous gift.
I ain't got a camera, though.
No problem! We can lend you one. I have a high-end single-lens reflex camera to give you.
Yeah? How much ya gonna charge me?
Oh, no. I'll loan it to you for free. I do need you to give me a way to reach you in case something happens, though.
(Guess there ain't any reason to turn him down. Might as well take up the offer.)
Yeah, I'll do it.
Great! Here's the camera.
You got a <Color:8>Borrowed Single-lens Reflex Camera<Color:Default>.
You can find me here during the campaign. Come back once you've shot five locations.
Good luck out there!
When you visit sightseeing spots around town, the Photograph action icon may appear. Press <Action:Button_Cross@Adventure> while this is displayed to take a photo.
You can view photos you've taken from City Exploration under Completion List in the Pause Menu. Once you take five photos, bring them to the Tourism Board staff member to receive a reward.

en: I guess my merchandise just isn't any good...
Welcome! I sell local specialties at a store nearby! Please come take a look!
(Nothing but senbei and manju... Pretty conventional stuff.)
(Nothing but senbei and manju... Pretty boring.)
(Nothin' but senbei and manju... Ain't all that exciting.)
(Senbei and manju... It doesn't look all that appealing.)
What do you think? Not to your liking?
You don't need to say anything. I can tell from your face that you don't see anything you like.
What am I going to do!? My supplier doesn't have anything decent, and I've already paid the rent on this store!
I've never even been on a trip myself! How am I supposed to know what souvenirs sell!?
I just saw on the TV that local specialties were all the rage! I thought I'd be knee-deep in cash by now!
You... wouldn't happen to be from out of town, would you?
Yeah, I came from Fukuoka.
Yeah, I'm from Osaka.
Yeah, I came from Hokkaido.
Yeah, I came here from Nagoya.
Actually, yes. I came from Osaka.
Perfect! Then you must know all about the local specialties there, right?
Could you bring me some of them? I know it's a huge favor, but I swear you'll be well rewarded!
Might be hard to believe, but I'm somewhat of a whiz at marketing. Wanna know why?
So you know those singles mixers? Those things are chock full of college students and business women, and let me tell you, those girls know all the hottest trends.
They've given me tons of information on what kinds of specialties I should be selling. I'll describe them to you, and you bring me items that match those descriptions.
I'll reward you well, of course. And your help would mean so much to me and my business!
Oh, and you don't need to go out of your way. Just stop by a store while you're doing your thing whenever you've got time.
I don't mind doing it on the side.
Yeah, I could do that at some point.
All right, if I remember.
I'll do it if I get something in return.
I'll look around if I get a chance.
Thank you! Well, I'll go and do some marketing research. Come and see me again sometime.
I'm currently looking for souvenirs from regional cities. If you have any, I'd gladly take them off your hands.
This is what I'm looking for right now.
That's absolutely perfect! Just what I was looking for!
Keep up the good work!
I'm afraid I don't need that right now. Do you have anything else?
The original spicy fish roe flavor from Fukuya, which has been dedicated to quality since it opened.
The secret to its enduring popularity is the tweaks they make based on customer feedback to fine-tune the flavor for each generation.
Each plump piece of cod roe is bursting with goodness and lets the flavors of the ingredients shine.
A mild-flavored spicy fish roe for those who don't like too much kick in their food.
By bringing down the signature spiciness a notch, you can enjoy the flavors of the roe even more.
Hot Emperor was created to answer the demand for a spicy fish roe packed with only the finest red chili peppers.
Seven different spices are mixed into a sophisticated blend that takes advantage of the characteristics of each, adding depth to the taste.
One bite sends waves of heat throughout the body, making this the perfect spicy fish roe for chili aficionados.
This product was created for customers who long for a taste of the old days.
The balance of flavorsome roasted chili peppers and salt recreates the original that first went on sale in 1949.
The heat catches up with you after a few bites, complementing its delicious flavor perfectly.
This confection features sweet Hokkaido beans enveloped in a soft, mochi-like shell. It has been a Hakata favorite for over thirty years.
It was awarded the Prime Minister's Prize at the 19th National Confectionery Exposition.
It has a natural, rustic flavor and remains one of the flagship Hakata confections of manufacturer Saemon.
Phrases from the Burabura theme song have entered the lexicon, and Hakata locals will even dance to it when it comes on.
